answer.rationale: The incumbent renewal keeps the integration stable and the delivery risk unchanged (primary objective). Memory_c1 shows this has worked across two cycles with no migration or delivery disruption. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. Memory_c4 shows renegotiating at renewal recovers real margin. Memory_c5 shows deferral is possible for non-critical items. Memory_c2 shows switching to a low-cost vendor is viable but carries onboarding risk. Memory_c3 shows adding a second source removes single-point-of-failure risk but does not directly cut cost. Given the 18% cost mandate and the 14-day contract expiry, the single highest-leverage, lowest-risk action is to renew with the incumbent but renegotiate terms (price, payment terms, volume commitment) to hit the cost target while keeping delivery stable and avoiding any onboarding or migration risk that the 94% assembly line cannot absorb.
